process.heading: How an Edstellar team coaching program runs.
process.description: Six steps take the team from sponsor discovery to a review and re-diagnostic. Your sponsor sees progress at every step; what is said in sessions stays in the room.

steps.label: Sponsor discovery
steps.title: Sponsor discovery
steps.description: The sponsor meets the Edstellar coaching consultant to describe the team, the challenge and what a successful program looks like. The focus area is agreed and the program is scoped.

steps.label: Team diagnostic
steps.title: Team diagnostic
steps.description: A short diagnostic with the team — either a survey or individual conversations — gives the coach a clear picture of the team's starting point before the first session.

steps.label: Kickoff session
steps.title: Kickoff session
steps.description: The coach meets the team, shares what the diagnostic found, agrees the focus area and the way of working for sessions together.

steps.label: Team coaching sessions
steps.title: Team coaching sessions
steps.description: Facilitated sessions of 60 to 90 minutes on the agreed focus area. The team does the work; the coach holds the space and the process.

steps.label: Actions between sessions
steps.title: Actions between sessions
steps.description: Each session ends with agreed actions the team takes back into their daily work. The coach follows up at the start of the next session.

steps.label: Review and re-diagnostic
steps.title: Review and re-diagnostic
steps.description: At the end of the program, the team reviews progress against the focus area. A re-diagnostic measures what has changed and agrees the next step.

items.question: What is team coaching?
items.answer: Team coaching is facilitated coaching with an intact group — a leadership team, a newly formed team or a cross-functional group — focused on the shared dynamics, agreements and habits that shape how they work together. Edstellar's team coaching is delivered in facilitated sessions of 60 to 90 minutes by a certified team coach.

items.question: Who is team coaching for?
items.answer: Team coaching is for leadership teams, newly formed teams that need to find their rhythm, cross-functional and project teams that work across organizational lines, and teams navigating a merger or restructure.

items.question: How many sessions does a team coaching program include?
items.answer: The number of sessions is agreed in the sponsor discovery and depends on the team's focus area and starting point. Most programs run four to six facilitated sessions over three to six months, plus a diagnostic and a final review.

items.question: What certifications do Edstellar team coaches hold?
items.answer: Every Edstellar team coach is certified by the International Coaching Federation (ICF) at PCC or MCC level, the International Coaching Community (ICC) or the European Mentoring and Coaching Council (EMCC), and is experienced in group coaching and team dynamics.

items.question: How does Edstellar select a team coach?
items.answer: Edstellar recommends certified team coaches based on the team's focus area, size, industry and the working language of the group. The sponsor reviews the recommendations and chooses a coach in the discovery session.

items.question: What does our sponsor see during team coaching?
items.answer: The sponsor sees sessions held, the focus area and progress against it, and the agreed actions the team carries forward. What is said in sessions stays between the team and the coach.

items.question: What are the six team coaching focus areas?
items.answer: Shared Purpose & Goals, Trust, Decision-Making, Healthy Conflict, Accountability and Collaboration Across Boundaries. The focus area is agreed in the discovery and diagnostic.

items.question: Is team coaching delivered virtually or in person?
items.answer: Edstellar delivers team coaching virtually. Sessions are facilitated live on video, scheduled to accommodate the team's time zones. In-person delivery can be discussed for teams in the same location.
